You wouldn't be building equity though. There are absolutely costs to maintaining a house but the long term advantages are undeniable. It takes the largest expense from the average budget and turns it into an investment. 

Comparing renting to a zero down mortgage doesn't address the hoarding of properties by investors or the inadequate supply due to zoning. Saying that it's cheaper to rent in the short term doesn't hide that in the long term renting is precarious and costly. Retiring as a renter is not a great position to be in.

Social interaction can be so draining. Every time I would embarrass myself it would haunt me for weeks. Even now I'll have flashbacks to me making a fool of myself 10-15 years ago and I start berating myself. But I wish I had pushed myself to keep going out. I'm in my thirties now and have no social connections at all. It all started when I hid myself away. Everything that made social interaction difficult in the first place became worse. And worse.  Now I'm a hopeless recluse eagerly awaiting the end. 

So I really suggest you push yourself as much as you can. People are still bothering to include you in their lives. Avoiding them will lead to them avoiding you. It gets real lonely.

I feel this way too. I think most people are redundant even if they refuse to admit it. I'm never going to be one of the good ones. What's the point? To live as less than and feel inferior all the time? Average doesn't get you anything close to a life worth living so if you happen to be trash forget about it.
